newsitem.title: USA: US High Court says punitive damages are taxable.
newsitem.headline: US High Court says punitive damages are taxable.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled Tuesday that punitive damages awarded in a personal injury lawsuit are taxable.

The justices, by a 6-3 vote, upheld a U.S. appeals court ruling that punitive damages should be included in taxable income. The ruling was a victory for the U.S. Justice Department, which argued that the damages should be taxed.
At issue was a section of the Internal Revenue Code that excludes from its definition of gross income any damages received "on account of personal injuries or sickness."

The case involved the family of a woman who died of toxic shock syndrome in 1983. The family won a punitive damage award of $10 million in a product liability suit against International Playtex Inc, the manufacturer of the tampons the woman used.

Writing for the high court, Justice Stephen Breyer said the punitive damages were not received "on account of personal injuries." He said punitive damages generally were awarded to punish reprehensible conduct and deter its future occurrence, not to compensate for injury.
